title: Between-animal synapse count differences repeat across sides after neuron gain correction in three adult fly connectomes
abstract: We tested whether count differences between adult fly connectomes repeat on both sides of the animals after neuron input and output gains are removed. We reused six matched count tables from three adult connectomes and fitted gains on separate connection folds. For connections with at least 64 synapses across four copies, left-right correlations of residual log count ratios were 0.641, 0.541 and 0.453 in the three animal pairs. When each copy had a positive count, the correlations were 0.360, 0.455 and 0.428. A linear model reduced excluded-connection prediction error by 13% to 21% in the positive-count samples. Count floors, clipping and deletion of any one identity kept the relation positive. Independent Poisson references did not reproduce it. Bilateral absence in one animal explained much of the larger all-count covariance, especially in one female/male comparison. The remaining variation has a shared bilateral component beyond one scale per neuron. Three animals cannot separate biology, contact geometry, matching errors and shared reconstruction effects. The animal pairs are not independent replications. We include code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and retrieval instructions; record-level source data stay external.
